svg.title: Goldschtein bat figure
svg.desc: Hierarchical von Mises-Uniform mixture modeling of sensory-deprivation homing trajectories in bats. Free-flying bats were translocated within their home range and tracked during homing flights to a known goal (either the roost "Home" or the Agamon Hula Lake region). Step headings were converted to a circular bearing error by subtracting the instantaneous distance-minimizing target bearing so that y=0 indicates perfect alignment toward the goal and y=+/-pi indicates movement directly away from the goal. We fit a hierarchical von Mises-Uniform mixture (vMU) in which each step is generated either by a directed von Mises component or an undirected uniform component, allowing treatments to affect the directed-component mean mu, directed-component concentration kappa, and the directed-step mixing weight omega. (a) Representative trajectories for roost and lake goals with translocation locations and signal dropouts indicated (scale bar, 1000 m). (b) A photo of a tagged bat, with the four treatment-sense combinations indicated. (c) Predictive model comparison using PSIS-LOO expected log predictive density (ELPD), contrasting a unimodal von Mises likelihood with the vMU; higher ELPD indicates better expected out-of-sample predictive performance. (d) ELPD difference (vMU minus von Mises), shown overall and within each treatment group. (e) Posterior predictive density at the goal direction (y*=0) under the fitted vMU, reported by treatment; the dashed vertical line indicates the uniform baseline density 1/(2pi). (f) Treatment-level directed-component von Mises densities on the circle (posterior mean and interval band). (g) Directed-component probability summarized along flights as a function of cumulative path distance from the endpoint (computed post hoc by smoothing posterior step-wise responsibilities); shaded bands indicate posterior uncertainty. (h) Example trajectories (one per treatment) colored by posterior mean directed-component probability (step-wise mixture responsibility). Additional per-flight posterior predictive checks, sensitivity analyses, and supplementary trajectory summaries are provided in the Supplementary Figures.
